body.statement: For every acyclic tree-shaped mixed graph \(G=(V,D,B)\), meaning that \((V,D)\) is a rooted directed tree while \(B\) is arbitrary, the Gupta--Bl\"aser algorithm decides in randomized polynomial time, for every \(e\in D\), whether \(\lambda_e\) has one, two, or infinitely many generic values. In the first two cases it returns, respectively, one or two fractional affine square-root terms of polynomials representing those values. Its polynomial-identity-testing error can be made at most any prescribed \(\delta\in(0,1)\).

source.locator: Sections 1.1--2.1, Algorithm 2, Theorem 27, and the running-time analysis immediately following Theorem 27
